title: The Shower That Became a Pool — Forensic Pathology, Diagnostic Verification & Real-World Injury/Illness Prevention

teenKit.tldr: An unexpected medical paradox turns a standard safety recommendation into a fatal hazard when a patient's body position alters the physics of a simple shower room. Forensic pathologists use peer-reviewed case data to decode how everyday built environments can unexpectedly trigger real-world disasters.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It forces us to realize that safety isn't just about static equipment like seatbelts, but about how our own bodies interact with the dynamic architecture around us.
keyTakeaways: Static safety devices like seatbelts rely on fixed physical properties, but architectural spaces can completely change their behavior based on human position.
Forensic pathology uses primary case records and diagnostic verification to piece together how everyday environments can turn lethal.
True safety planning requires anticipating how human medical vulnerabilities and architectural designs intersect in the real world.

vocab.meaning: The medical science of investigating sudden or unexpected deaths by examining the body and analyzing medical evidence.
The strict process of confirming a medical diagnosis using physical evidence, lab tests, and clinical data rather than guesswork.
A safety feature like a seatbelt or a guardrail that does its job through fixed physical materials without needing constant human monitoring.
The human-made spaces, buildings, and architecture where we live, move, and interact every single day.
